text: Okay. Quick question.
If I handed you twenty dollars right now...
what would make you happier? Spending it on you... or on someone else?
Yeah. Most people pick, on me.
Researchers tested it. And most people are wrong. Twice.
This one's a nice one, I promise.
So. Some researchers in Vancouver ran a little experiment on a university campus.
First, they asked: how happy are you this morning?
Then they handed over an envelope. Five dollars, or twenty.
With one rule. Spend it by five p.m. today.
Half of them had to spend it on themselves. A bill, or a little treat.
The other half had to spend it on someone else. A gift, or a donation.
That evening, the phone rings. So... how happy are you now?
The people who spent on someone else were happier.
And the twenty dollars? Made no difference. Five worked just as well.
Here's the funny part.
They asked another group of students to guess what would happen.
Most guessed spending on yourself would feel better. And that twenty beats five.
And in real life? A survey of over six hundred Americans found people spend more than ten times as much on themselves as on others.
But the me money wasn't linked to happiness at all. The others money was.
Even with a work bonus of about five thousand dollars, what mattered weeks later wasn't how big it was. It was how much of it went to other people.
And this might start really early.
In another study, toddlers, not even two years old, got a bowl of crackers.
Then a puppet named Monkey showed up, hungry.
They looked happier giving Monkey a cracker than getting one themselves.
Happiest of all? When it was their own cracker.
Now, honesty time.
When other teams repeated the envelope test, the effect was smaller. One found no clear difference at all.
It showed up best when people actually spent on someone. Not when they just remembered doing it.
So it's not magic. But it's real, and it's cheap to try.
So here's what you can try this week.
One. The five dollar test. Spend five on someone else, on purpose, and notice how you feel tonight.
Two. Give your spending a tiny others line. Even one coffee a month.
Three. This gift season, swap one thing for you for one small thing for someone else.
Money can buy you a better day.
It just works better when it's not for you.
Subscribe, and go find someone to spend five dollars on.
